record.original_question: Under reasonable growth conditions on the stored-energy function W, determine whether global minimizers or suitably defined local minimizers of I(y)=∫Ω W(Dy) dx satisfy the weak Euler-Lagrange equation ∫Ω DAW(Dy) · Dφ dx = 0 for all smooth test fields φ that vanish on the displacement boundary.

evidence.quote: we obtain the weak form of the Euler-Lagrange equation for I
Problem 5. Prove or disprove that, under reasonable growth conditions on W, global or suitably defined local minimizers of I satisfy the weak form (2.4) of the Euler-Lagrange equation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary, representing the reference configuration of an elastic body, and let $\partial\Omega = \partial_1\Omega \cup \partial_2\Omega$ be a disjoint decomposition into a displacement (Dirichlet) part $\partial_1\Omega$ and a traction-free part $\partial_2\Omega$. Let $W:M^{n\times n}_+\to\mathbb{R}$ be a stored-energy function defined on the set $M^{n\times n}_+$ of $n\times n$ matrices with positive determinant, assumed $C^1$, and satisfying "reasonable" growth conditions (for example, polyconvexity together with a coercivity estimate $W(A)\ge c|A|^p - C$ for some $p\ge 1$, and a growth bound on the derivative $D_AW$ that is compatible with the function space in which minimizers live). Consider the elastic energy
$$ I(y) \;=\; \int_\Omega W(Dy(x))\,dx, $$
defined on the admissible class
$$ \mathcal{A} \;=\; \{\, y\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n) : \det Dy>0\ \text{a.e.},\ y|_{\partial_1\Omega} = y_0 \,\}, $$
where $y_0$ is a prescribed boundary datum.

Prove or disprove: every global minimizer $y\in\mathcal{A}$ of $I$ (and, more generally, every suitably defined local minimizer) satisfies the weak form of the Euler-Lagrange equation
$$ \int_\Omega D_A W(Dy(x)) : D\varphi(x)\,dx \;=\; 0 $$
for every smooth test field $\varphi\in C^\infty_c(\Omega\cup\partial_2\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ vanishing on $\partial_1\Omega$.
artifact.category_tag: Calculus of variations in nonlinear elasticity
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a longstanding open problem in the calculus of variations and nonlinear elasticity. Known one-dimensional counterexamples (the Lavrentiev phenomenon) show that without restrictions minimizers need not satisfy the Euler-Lagrange equation, and partial positive results are available for special growth conditions (Ball–Murat, Bauman–Owen–Phillips, and recent work on incompressible minimizers), but the general case under "reasonable" growth on W remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: One-dimensional variational problems whose minimizers do not satisfy the Euler-Lagrange equation (Ball & Mizel)
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of variational problems whose minimizers fail to satisfy the Euler-Lagrange equation.
status_evidence.claim: Shows that without careful growth hypotheses minimizers need not satisfy the Euler-Lagrange equation.

status_evidence.title: On derivation of Euler–Lagrange equations for incompressible energy-minimizers
status_evidence.snippet: Derives Euler–Lagrange equations for volume-preserving minimizers, partially addressing the long-standing problem.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress in the incompressible case.

status_evidence.title: Progress and puzzles in nonlinear elasticity (J. M. Ball)
status_evidence.snippet: Updated discussion of open problems including derivation of the Euler–Lagrange equation.
status_evidence.claim: Status reported as still open in later survey.
